tasks.short: Log what a shipper promised and where the collection stands.

today.trigger: A call ends, or a shipper mail changes a promise, a dispute or the next step.
steps: Find the debtor in AFAS Profit and open the last note.
Write who was reached, what was said, any amount and date, and whether a dispute was raised.
Copy the same facts into an Excel follow-up list, because the nightly Power BI extract does not total free-text notes.
Set an Outlook reminder for the promise date.
drudgery: Typing one outcome into AFAS, Excel and Outlook
Free-text notes the nightly dashboard cannot total
today.time_sinks: Most of the 153 hours goes to finding the debtor and writing the same outcome in more than one place.

lenses.faster: Retyping the outcome into Excel and Outlook disappears, and the AFAS note is drafted from the officer's few words or from the mail. A no-contact line posts on its own, and a promise, an amount or a dispute takes about a minute to confirm.
lenses.autonomous: A dictated call outcome or a shipper mail starts it, and a no-contact line is written to the debtor with no one present. The officer is the gate for any line that carries an amount, a promise date or a dispute.
lenses.ambitious: FP&A gets a same-day log of promises and disputes, a service it does not have while cash is rebuilt from the nightly extract. Demand for a weekly cash-in figure grows if keeping the log is cheap, because the Finance Director's close depends on a forecast the business trusts.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing the same outcome into AFAS, Excel and Outlook. The officer wants the time for shippers who dispute a load.
lenses.options: Coding the same call as a promise or as a dispute changes whether the next reminder goes and whether FP&A counts the cash. Where the words are ambiguous the draft shows both codes and the officer picks one.
lenses.altitude: Logging shrinks to a short review of the money notes. The officer gains a coded history they can stand behind with FP&A, and the job becomes more expert because the code is a judgment of what the shipper actually said.
reach: The FP&A analyst's retype of promises into the cash forecast, once this officer learns the categories that forecast already uses.

tasks.human_edge: The officer heard the call and knows whether a vague agreement to look at an invoice was a promise. The draft has to leave a polite delay as a delay, and it has to leave a dispute unstated when the shipper did not raise one.
tasks.pattern_why: The balance and the due date are already fields in AFAS. The work left is a messy call or mail, and one model call can turn it into a note with outcome, amount, date and dispute flag that the officer can check.

in_practice.trigger: The officer dictates a few words at the end of a call, or a shipper mail arrives that changes the collection status.
steps: Write the draft only from those words or from that mail, into fixed fields: outcome, amount, date, dispute flag, next step.
Post a no-contact line to the AFAS debtor dossier.
Hold any line with an amount, a promise date or a dispute for the officer to confirm.
Drop the Excel follow-up list and the separate Outlook reminder once the promise date is a field the worklist can read.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer confirms every note that records money, a date or a dispute before it is treated as fact.
data_needed: Debtor number
The officer's words or the mail text
Open invoice numbers
Any existing dispute flag
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS debtor dossier, with the source text kept beside the coded note.

evidence.claim: Among 336 Dutch finance and credit professionals, 30% name manual work in Excel, mail and exports as the biggest cash-flow problem.

A wrong fact early in the file, including a wrong letter, wrong interest or costs, or terms that were never handed over, surfaces when the claim is tested later. Courts test consumer claims of their own motion.
A short dictated outcome can be mapped to fixed fields. Whether AFAS at Noordhaven already has those fields is not established.

risks: A note that later goes to a lawyer can be wrong if vague language is upgraded into a promise or a dispute.
Notes that name a sole trader or a private accounts-payable clerk are personal data under the AVG and need restricted access and a retention rule.
Recording the officer's calls to feed the note would be employee monitoring and a matter for the works council. A note the officer dictates after the call keeps that off the table.
research_questions: What share of notes are no-contact, a promise with an amount, or a dispute, and is that already a field in AFAS or only free text?
Do the lawyers or bailiffs Noordhaven uses treat the AFAS note as the file, and would they reject a note the officer had not confirmed?
How many debtors are sole traders, so that the note is personal data under the AVG?

tasks.short: Find which shippers are overdue and who to call.

today.trigger: Several times a day the officer checks who is past due before calling, and again before a warehouse cutoff.
steps: Export open items from AFAS or refresh the Power BI ageing page from the nightly extract.
Remove lines that the latest Rabobank import has already covered but that AFAS has not matched.
Sort the rest in Excel by age, amount and broken promises.
Build the day's call list and skip accounts already marked in dispute.
drudgery: Rebuilding the ageing export more than once a day
Crossing the bank import against the call list by hand
today.time_sinks: The export, the clean-up of cash already received, and the sort take most of the 142 hours.

lenses.faster: The export, the strike-off of cash already in the bank, and the manual sort disappear. What stays is about ten minutes on the list, plus a change of order when a shipper's situation is not in the fields.
lenses.autonomous: Each Rabobank import and each refresh of open items rebuilds the overdue list with no one present. The officer is the gate for a credit hold and for any reorder the fields do not support.
lenses.ambitious: The planning desks at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo see a credit-hold flag on the day a promise breaks, a group that today hears about a stop later by mail. Demand from those desks grows if the flag stays current at low effort, because a missed hold loads another shipment for a shipper who is not paying.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the ageing export. The officer wants the choice of who to call before the cutoff.
lenses.options: A list ordered by broken promise, by age, or by euros changes who is called before the warehouse cutoff. The officer switches the order when a large shipper and an older small one both qualify and the relationship decides it.
lenses.altitude: The day starts from a list that is already current after the bank import. The officer gains the right to put a broken promise ahead of an older small balance, and monitoring becomes a short expert check.
reach: The controller's routine question on who is overdue, once this officer learns the materiality the controller uses at month close.

tasks.human_edge: The officer knows which shipper is in a live rate argument with sales, and which overdue balance is only a missing document. The sort does not know that, so the officer changes the order when the fields and the relationship disagree.
tasks.pattern_why: Age, amount, a promise date and a dispute flag are queries on AFAS fields, and a rule can build the list after the bank import. A model does not make the ageing truer.

in_practice.trigger: A Rabobank statement is imported, or open items change during the day.
steps: Rebuild the list from live AFAS open items, skipping the nightly Power BI extract for same-day work.
Drop debtors whose unmatched cash covers the overdue invoices.
Rank the rest by broken promise, then by the rule the controller has agreed.
Show a proposed credit hold to the officer, and publish the hold to the three sites only after approval.
Leave dispute accounts off the call list and on the dispute queue.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves any credit hold before a site can see it, and reorders the list when a known shipper should be called or skipped.
data_needed: Open invoices, due dates and amounts
Promise date and dispute flag
Unmatched Rabobank lines on that debtor
Shipper name and the site that loads their freight
in_practice.logs_to: The worklist history in AFAS, including why a debtor was listed or held.

evidence.claim: Of 336 Dutch finance and credit professionals, 81% explain DSO after the fact, and half plan cash-in no more than two weeks ahead.

AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums, and leaves the misses to a person, so an overdue list that ignores those misses will chase cash already received.
Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is high-risk under Annex III point 5(b), and those Annex III duties apply from 2 December 2027. A sole-trader haulier counts as a natural person.

risks: A list that ignores unmatched bank lines will have the officer call a shipper who has already paid.
Ranking this list is allowed. Scoring the creditworthiness of a sole-trader haulier would be a high-risk use under the EU AI Act from 2 December 2027.
A hold flag the sites obey can stop freight for a shipper sales has decided to keep, so the mandate has to name who may set it.
research_questions: Can the officer run a live open-item list from AFAS during the day, or is the nightly Power BI extract the only ageing they can see?
What share of overdue euros sits with the ten largest shippers, and would a broken-promise rule change the order the officer would choose?
Is there already a credit-hold flag that planning at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo can see without a mail?
How many debtors are sole traders, so a future score would fall under Annex III 5(b)?

tasks.short: Remind late shippers by mail and call them for payment.

today.trigger: An invoice is past its due date and the officer's list says it is time to chase.
steps: Open the shipper in AFAS and check for a dispute or a payment the bank import has not yet cleared.
Send the standard Dutch reminder from Outlook, or write a one-off mail when the amount looks wrong.
Call the shipper's accounts-payable contact when mail has not produced a payment.
Write the attempt on the debtor.
drudgery: Copying invoice numbers and amounts into reminder mails
Looking up the right accounts-payable address
today.time_sinks: The calls take the largest share of the 130 hours. Preparing the mail and finding the right contact take most of what remains.

lenses.faster: Finding the account and drafting the standard reminder disappear, and those mails go out on the step rule. The phone calls stay at today's length, and a first letter or a letter that states interest takes a few minutes to approve.
lenses.autonomous: An invoice that reaches a reminder step, with no open dispute and no unmatched cash on that debtor, sends the standard template with no one present. The officer is the gate for a first letter, for any letter that adds interest or the EUR 40 compensation, for a sole trader, and for every phone call.
lenses.ambitious: Smaller and seasonal shippers, who today wait behind the large balances, get the standard reminder on the due-date rule. Demand for that cadence grows if it is cheap, because sales keeps opening small accounts and those balances now go quiet.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting invoice numbers into reminder mails. The officer wants the phone call with the shipper's accounts-payable manager.
lenses.options: A plain reminder, a reminder that adds commercial interest and the EUR 40 compensation, or a phone call changes what the shipper is told and what Noordhaven can claim later. The rule proposes one path and the officer switches it when sales is in a live rate talk with that shipper.
lenses.altitude: Standard reminders leave the desk, and the week keeps the calls plus a short approval queue. The officer keeps the right to stop a letter, to add interest and the EUR 40, or to call, so the contact work that remains is more expert.
reach: The bookkeeper's resend of an invoice a shipper says never arrived, once this officer learns which AFAS layout is the official invoice.

tasks.human_edge: The officer makes the call and judges the tone for a shipper Noordhaven wants to keep. The officer also approves the first letter and any letter that states interest or the EUR 40, because a wrong amount is hard to undo once the shipper has it.
tasks.pattern_why: The reminder step, the due date, commercial interest and the EUR 40 compensation are rules, and the standard letter is a fixed template. A model would vary a letter that should stay identical.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice reaches the next reminder step in the calendar the controller has agreed, and the debtor has no open dispute and no unmatched cash covering it.
steps: Send the standard Dutch template, naming the invoices and the principal only.
Hold the first letter on a new debtor, every letter that adds interest or the EUR 40, every letter to a sole trader, and any text that is not the template.
Put the debtor on the call list when the mail step is exhausted.
Stop the sequence when a dispute is opened or when cash covers the invoices.
Keep an English template only where finance has approved the wording.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves the held letters before they send, and places every phone call. Noordhaven sends its own reminders.
data_needed: Invoice number, date, amount and the due date printed on it
Reminder step already sent
Dispute flag and unmatched cash
Whether the debtor is a sole trader or a company
The approved Dutch template and the terms that were handed to the shipper
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS reminder history and the sent mail stored on the debtor file.

evidence.claim: For a commercial debt, statutory interest runs from the agreed due date, or from 30 days after the invoice if no due date was agreed, and at least EUR 40 compensation is due without any reminder.
Mistakes that show up in court start in the file: a wrong first letter, interest or costs miscalculated, or terms that were never handed over. Courts test consumer claims of their own motion.

Since 1 October 2026 a debtor who is a natural person, including a sole trader or a partnership, owes no collection costs or further interest when the party sending reminders on another's behalf is not registered. The debt itself stands. Bailiffs and lawyers are exempt. Chasing one's own invoices is not described as covered.

risks: A first letter with the wrong interest, a wrong EUR 40, or terms the shipper never received is the error that surfaces when the claim is tested.

If Noordhaven later lets an agency send reminders, an unregistered agency puts costs and further interest at risk for sole traders and partnerships under the Wki. The debt stands, and bailiffs and lawyers are exempt.
Many transport invoices may carry no agreed due date, so the 30-day rule has to be read from the invoice in front of the officer, not assumed.
research_questions: Which reminder steps does Noordhaven send today, and what share of invoices have no due date agreed on the document?
What share of reminder text is an unchanged template, and what share states interest or the EUR 40?
Does Noordhaven send every reminder itself? If an agency sends any, is that agency on the Wki register?
What share of shippers need an English letter, which a Dutch-only template would get wrong?

tasks.short: Answer a shipper's question about an invoice or a balance.

today.trigger: A shipper mails or calls about a balance, an invoice, or a payment they say they made.
steps: Read the Outlook thread and open the debtor in AFAS.
Pull the invoice PDF and, when they ask for proof of delivery, ask the site on Teams.
Reply with the balance, the open invoices, or the document.
Move the mail onto the dispute list when it is really a complaint about the load or the rate.
drudgery: Searching the dossier for an invoice PDF
Waiting on a warehouse colleague for a proof of delivery
today.time_sinks: Finding documents, and waiting on Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo, takes as long as writing the reply across these 126 hours.

lenses.faster: Searching AFAS and the debtor folder for a statement or an invoice copy disappears. Approving the draft takes a few minutes, and a missing proof of delivery still waits on the site.
lenses.autonomous: A shipper mail about the account starts it, and the agent gathers a statement, an invoice copy, or a proof of delivery that is already on the file and drafts the reply. The officer approves every send, and a dispute or a missing proof stops with the officer.
lenses.ambitious: The shipper's accounts-payable clerk gets the balance, the invoice and any filed proof of delivery in one same-day reply, a service that today reaches the accounts who chase hardest. Demand grows if that reply is cheap, because clerks will bring forward the mismatches that are blocking their payment run.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching the dossier for a PDF. The officer wants the mails that are real complaints, where a document is not the answer.
lenses.options: A reply that the invoice stands, with the proof attached, and a reply that the line is paused pending the site, lead to different payments. The draft includes the second version only when a damage note or a missing proof is already on the file, and the officer picks.
lenses.altitude: Document replies become a short approval queue in the day. The officer keeps the right to refuse a draft that would admit a claim, and more of the week goes to real complaints, so the job is more expert.
reach: The accounts-receivable bookkeeper's replies that only attach a statement or an invoice copy, once this officer learns where those bookkeepers file a remittance.

tasks.human_edge: The officer decides whether the mail is a question or a claim. The agent may attach a document already on the file. It has to stop short of conceding damage, waiting time or a rate, and it has to stop short of describing a proof of delivery the site has not provided.
tasks.pattern_why: The mail decides the path: a statement, an invoice copy, a proof of delivery, a payment already received, or a dispute, and the proof may simply be absent. The sequence is chosen per mail, and a person approves before anything is sent.

in_practice.trigger: A mail arrives on the collections mailbox asking about a balance, an invoice or a payment.
steps: Class the mail against the debtor's open items and the documents already in the AFAS dossier or the SharePoint debtor folder.
Draft a reply that attaches only those documents and states only amounts AFAS shows.
If the mail alleges damage, waiting time, a refused load, a rate or a surcharge, or if the proof of delivery is not filed, stop and leave it with the officer.
Send only after the officer approves, on the same thread.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves every outbound reply. The agent does not mail the warehouses and does not mail the shipper.
data_needed: The inbound mail
Open items and matched cash on the debtor
Invoice PDFs and any proof of delivery already filed
Dispute notes already on the file
in_practice.logs_to: The outbound mail and the documents attached, stored on the AFAS debtor dossier.

evidence.claim: Genpact's accounts-receivable suite keeps people on validation and on complex decisions. The same page's figures for productivity and disputes are indicative estimates, and the named buyer, FLSmidth, has no published result.
A wrong statement of the claim in early correspondence is the class of error that surfaces when the file is later tested.
Noordhaven's named systems do not include a transport system, so a proof of delivery is available to finance only when someone has filed it.

risks: A reply that admits liability, or that attaches another load's proof, creates a dispute Noordhaven then has to unwind.
If most questions need a proof of delivery that is not filed, the agent stops and the time saving shrinks to statement and invoice-copy mail.
Mails about a sole trader can be personal data under the AVG. The reply goes back on the same thread, to the address that wrote.
research_questions: What share of shipper mail asks for a statement, an invoice copy or a filed proof, and what share is a dispute about damage, waiting time or a rate?
Where do proofs of delivery sit today, and can finance open them without a Teams message to the warehouse?
In a sample of twenty replies, how often would the officer reject the draft?

tasks.short: Get a shipper to pay, agree a plan, or settle a damage claim.

today.trigger: A shipper disputes an amount, misses a promise, or asks for more time to pay.
steps: Pull the invoices, the earlier reminders and any proof of delivery already on the file.
Ask the site, usually on Teams, what happened on the load: damage, waiting time, or a refused delivery.
Call the shipper and ask for payment, a date, or a clear statement of the dispute.
Agree a short plan or a credit only inside the finance mandate, and write the outcome on the debtor.
drudgery: Chasing a proof of delivery across a site before the call can start
Rebuilding the invoice story from notes and old mail
today.time_sinks: The call is the work. Waiting on the sites for the load facts is the long gap before it, across these 124 hours.

lenses.faster: Collecting invoices, reminders and any proof already filed disappears from the start of the call. The call stays the same length, and a plan or a credit still needs the conversation plus the controller where the mandate says so.
lenses.autonomous: A reply that disputes the amount, breaks a promise or asks for time assembles a brief from what is already filed, with no one present. The officer is the gate for the call, the plan and any credit, and the controller is the gate above the written mandate.
lenses.ambitious: The site managers at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a weekly list of invoices blocked by damage, waiting time or a missing proof of delivery, which they do not get today. Demand for that list grows if it is cheap to keep, because those causes now sit with the officer and the sites cannot see which load is holding cash.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing a warehouse for a proof before dialling. The officer wants the negotiation itself.
lenses.options: A short instalment plan, a credit hold on the next load, and a partial credit for damage produce different cash and different service. The officer chooses inside the mandate, with the file on screen, and the controller decides above it.
lenses.altitude: Calls start with the load facts already on screen, so more of the week is the conversation. The officer keeps the right to offer a plan, a hold or a credit inside the mandate, and the work becomes more expert because preparation no longer crowds out the negotiation.
reach: The controller's first draft of a payment-plan note, once this officer learns the written mandate for plans and credits. The controller keeps the decision above that mandate.

tasks.human_edge: The officer negotiates and can judge what the shipper will actually pay. A plan, a credit or a hold is a commercial decision inside the controller's mandate, and the officer stays responsible for what was agreed on the call.
tasks.pattern_why: The path of the conversation is not known before the shipper speaks. A copilot can put the filed facts on screen, and the officer leads the call.

in_practice.trigger: A debtor is on the call list for a broken promise, a dispute, or a request for time.
steps: Assemble the brief from AFAS invoices, reminder history, notes, and any proof or damage mail already filed.
Show the open amount, what the shipper has already said, and the gap where a proof is missing.
Leave damage, waiting time, rate and surcharge claims for the officer to take to the site.
Record the outcome the officer dictates: payment date, plan, hold, or credit.
Route a plan or a credit above the controller's mandate to the controller before it is confirmed to the shipper.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer conducts the call and agrees any plan, hold or credit. The controller approves above the written mandate. The copilot sends nothing.
data_needed: Invoices, payments and reminder history
Filed proofs of delivery and damage notes
The controller's written mandate for plans and credits
The shipper's last stated position
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS debtor dossier, with the officer's name on any plan or credit, and the controller's name where the mandate required it.

evidence.claim: Genpact's accounts-receivable suite describes people as remaining on validation and complex decision-making. Its figures, including faster disputes, are indicative estimates only, and FLSmidth has no published result.
The dispute file that matters here is delivery proof, a damage claim and surcharges. That mix is not measured for Noordhaven.
Commercial interest and the minimum EUR 40 compensation have a statutory basis, so a negotiated figure in a call note has to stay separate from those statutory amounts.

risks: A suggested plan can talk the officer into a credit the file does not support.
A brief that states a load fact the site has not confirmed will be repeated to the shipper as if it were known.
A plan agreed on the phone and left out of AFAS will be missed by the next reminder and by the cash forecast.
research_questions: What share of overdue euros is tied to damage, waiting time, a missing proof or a rate dispute, against a shipper who is simply late?
Who may agree a payment plan or a credit today, and is that mandate written down with a limit?
How long do Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo take to answer a request for a proof of delivery or a damage note?

tasks.short: Post money received to the right shipper invoices.

today.trigger: A Rabobank statement is imported and AFAS leaves lines unmatched, or a shipper pays against a collection promise.
steps: Open the unmatched bank lines in AFAS.
Search Outlook for a remittance advice that lists invoice numbers.
Split the receipt across invoices, often trying combinations in Excel first.
Leave short pays and unknown payers for a closer look with a bookkeeper.
drudgery: Reading remittance mails for invoice numbers
Testing which invoices sum to the amount received
today.time_sinks: Lines AFAS already matches do not sit in these 123 hours. The hours go to remittances, short pays and payments with no reference.

lenses.faster: Hunting the remittance thread and trying combinations in Excel disappears when the invoice numbers in the mail sum to the bank line. Short pays, unknown payers and sums that do not match stay, at a few minutes each.
lenses.autonomous: An unmatched Rabobank line starts it. AFAS posts what its own rules match, and a proposal from the remittance posts only when every invoice number it uses appears in the mail and the invoices sum to the line. The officer handles every other line.
lenses.ambitious: The controller and the FP&A analysts get collection cash applied on the day of the Rabobank import, including split remittances, so the close is not waiting on a clearing pile. Demand for that same-day application grows at month end if reading the remittances is cheap, because days to close is the finance aim.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss testing invoice combinations in Excel. The part worth keeping is recognising a short pay that is really a damage deduction.
lenses.options: Applying a short pay to a named invoice, leaving it unallocated, or parking it against an open damage claim changes the balance and the dispute list. The officer chooses when the remittance and the invoices do not agree.
lenses.altitude: Unmatched receipts become a short queue of proposals plus the lines that will not match. The officer gains the right to park a short pay as a dispute, which is a more expert reading of the receipt than forcing a match.
reach: The bookkeeper's allocation of collection receipts that AFAS did not match, once this officer learns the bank-allocation screen and the VAT coding of a short pay.

tasks.human_edge: The officer recognises a payment that is short because the shipper deducted damage or a surcharge. Posting that line as a clean receipt hides the dispute and flatters the ageing.
tasks.pattern_why: AFAS already applies the rules for payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first, so those lines need no model. One model call can read the remittance mail that those rules cannot, and a sum check makes the proposal testable.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS leaves a Rabobank receipt unmatched after its own matching rules.
steps: Search the debtor's Outlook thread for a remittance mail or PDF.
Propose an allocation only with invoice numbers that appear in that document.
Post automatically when those invoices belong to the same debtor and sum exactly to the bank line.
Hold short pays, unknown payers, sums that miss, and any invoice number that belongs to another debtor.
Use one queue shared with the accounts-receivable bookkeepers, with a single owner on each line.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer or the owning bookkeeper posts every held line. Exact, fully supported matches post on the rule and are sampled.
data_needed: Unmatched bank line: amount, date, IBAN, reference
Remittance mail or PDF
Open invoices and debtor IBANs
A damage or short-pay note if one is already on the debtor
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS cash-application log, with the remittance kept beside any model proposal.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches bank lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums, and sends the misses to a person.
Genpact markets touchless cash application, with an 'up to 80%' figure labelled as an indicative estimate, staff kept on validation, and no result published for the named buyer FLSmidth.

risks: A proposal that posts without the sum check can apply a damage deduction as if it were a clean payment.
A model can offer an invoice number that exists but was not in the remittance. The post rule requires the number to be present in the source text and the sum to match exactly.
The three bookkeepers post receipts too. Two queues on the same bank line will double-apply it or leave each person assuming the other has it.
research_questions: What share of Rabobank lines does AFAS match today, and what amount is left unmatched in a normal week?
Of the remainder, how many have a remittance mail or PDF in Outlook that names invoice numbers?
How often is a short pay a damage or surcharge deduction that should stay open as a dispute?
Who owns an unmatched line today when both this officer and a bookkeeper could post it?

tasks.short: Update billing details and close accounts that are finished.

today.trigger: A shipper sends a new billing address or invoice mailbox, post comes back, or a company looks inactive.
steps: Read the mail and open the debtor in AFAS.
Check the KvK number when the legal name or the existence of the company is in doubt.
Type the new address or mailbox onto the debtor.
Ask the accountant before closing anything when a sole trader has died or a company is dissolved.
drudgery: Retyping addresses and mailboxes from mail into AFAS
Chasing invoices that came back from an old mailbox
today.time_sinks: Each change is small. The 71 hours add up in interruptions, and a wrong IBAN or a dissolved company costs much more when it is found late.

lenses.faster: Retyping a clearly labelled new mailbox or address disappears, and the KvK check runs on a schedule. A legal name, an IBAN, a dissolution or a death still takes a short approval, and an unclear mail takes the same typing as today.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled KvK check or a mail with a new billing detail starts it, and a labelled mailbox or address change lands on a sample list. The officer approves a legal name, an IBAN, a dissolution or a death before AFAS changes, and the ledger stays in place when invoicing is blocked.
lenses.ambitious: Sole-trader hauliers whose KvK registration is dissolved get a block before the next invoice, a group that today stays open until a letter comes back. Demand does not grow if the check is cheap: there are few such debtors, and the value is a file that stops in time.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping mailboxes into AFAS. The careful moment worth keeping is closing a sole trader's account when the person has died or the business has stopped.
lenses.options: Writing a new invoice mailbox, changing the legal name from the KvK, or blocking a dissolved registration changes whether the next invoice goes out. Dissolution, a death and any IBAN change wait for the officer.
lenses.altitude: Address mail becomes a proposed field change, and the KvK check is no longer a special effort. The officer gains a clear right to block a dissolved number and to refuse an IBAN change, which is more expert work than retyping.
reach: The bookkeeper's updates to debtor billing addresses, once this officer learns which AFAS fields stay locked after an invoice has been sent.

tasks.human_edge: The officer confirms a dissolved company, a death, or a new IBAN before the master record changes. Those facts decide whether Noordhaven may still invoice or chase, and a living sole trader's details are personal data under the AVG.
tasks.pattern_why: A KvK status, a labelled address block and a block on a dissolved number are rules, and a form can write them to AFAS. A model is worth adding only if most changes arrive as unstructured mail.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly KvK check finds a changed or dissolved number, or a mail arrives with a new billing address or invoice mailbox.
steps: Match the mail to the debtor and propose only fields that are labelled in the mail, such as invoice email or postal address.
Write those proposed fields to a sample list the officer reviews.
Queue legal name, IBAN, dissolution and death for an explicit approval before AFAS changes.
On approval of a dissolution or a death, block new invoices and new reminders.
Leave the ledger rows in place for the retention period the accountant sets.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer approves every change of legal name, IBAN, dissolution or death. Routine mailbox and address changes are sampled. A second person confirms an IBAN change.
data_needed: Debtor KvK number and legal name
Current billing address, invoice mailbox and IBAN
The inbound mail
KvK status of the number
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS debtor audit trail, including who approved an IBAN, a legal name or a block.

evidence.claim: The KvK trade register is the public source for whether a Dutch company exists and for its registered name. How Noordhaven stores KvK numbers on debtors is not established.
A sole trader who is alive is a natural person, so billing details of that debtor are personal data under the AVG. A dissolved company's register extract is a company record.

risks: A wrong billing address sends invoices and reminders to a stranger, and that is an AVG incident when the document identifies a sole trader.
An IBAN change requested only by mail is a known fraud pattern, so it needs a second person.
Deleting a deceased sole trader's ledger, which this task's standard wording calls purging, can break the fiscal retention of the books. Block invoicing and keep the ledger.
research_questions: How many billing-detail changes arrive in a month, and how many are a labelled address against free text?
How many debtors are sole traders or partnerships, and how many stored KvK numbers are already dissolved?
Who may change an IBAN today, and is there a second-person check?
How long does finance keep a closed debtor, and who may block invoicing while the ledger stays?

tasks.short: Stop new loads and hand the file over when chasing fails.

today.trigger: Reminders and calls have produced no payment, no dispute is open, and the balance is still due.
steps: Pull invoices, terms from SharePoint, reminders, notes and any proof of delivery into a pack.
Tell the site or customer service, by mail or Teams, not to load the next order.
Send the pack to a lawyer, a bailiff or a collection agency and answer their questions.
Check whether a credit insurer has to be told, where a policy exists.
drudgery: Assembling the same pack of invoices, terms and reminders by hand
Filling documents the lawyer asks for after the first send
today.time_sinks: Building the pack and filling gaps take most of the 60 hours. Choosing to hand the file over is short beside the assembly.

lenses.faster: Collating invoices, terms, reminders, notes and filed proofs into a pack disappears. Reading the pack and choosing the path takes the same short decision as today, and a thin file goes back until the facts are in it.
lenses.autonomous: The last internal reminder step, with no dispute and with the balance still open, starts the pack, and the agent assembles it with no one present. The officer chooses a hold, a bailiff, a lawyer or a registered agency, and releases the pack.
lenses.ambitious: The external lawyer or bailiff receives a complete pack on the day internal steps end, which makes smaller balances practical to hand over where the preparation previously cost more than the fee. Demand for those smaller hand-overs grows if the pack is cheap, and only for balances the controller agrees are worth the fee.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss collating PDFs. The officer wants the decision to hold, to wait or to hand the file over, and a clean first conversation with the lawyer.
lenses.options: A credit hold, a hand-over to a bailiff or lawyer, and a hand-over to a registered agency are different costs and a different tone with the shipper. The pack is the same and the officer chooses the path. An insurer is notified only where a policy is in force.
lenses.altitude: The week contains ready packs, so the afternoon is no longer spent collating. The officer gains the right to choose hold, bailiff, lawyer or registered agency, and to send a thin file back, so the escalation work becomes more expert.
reach: The accountant's assembly of the open-invoice schedule for an external lawyer, once this officer learns the schedule the accountant will stand behind.

tasks.human_edge: The officer decides whether to escalate, and knows which shipper relationship a writ would burn. A lawyer or a bailiff stays responsible for what is filed. Syncasso's own account of draft summons still leaves the review with a legal professional and the writ with the bailiff.
tasks.pattern_why: The pack is a fixed set of documents, but the path is not: hold, wait, bailiff, lawyer, or a registered agency, and only some debtors have an insurer to notify. The agent assembles the file and a person chooses before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: The last internal reminder step has passed, no dispute is open, unmatched cash does not cover the balance, and the balance is above the line the controller has set for a pack.
steps: Assemble invoices, the terms that were handed over, the reminder history, the notes and any filed proof.
Flag a file as thin when the terms, the interest basis or the proof the claim needs are missing.
Show the officer the options: credit hold, bailiff, lawyer, or an agency, plus an insurer notice where a policy is on the debtor.
Check the Wki register when the debtor is a natural person and the proposed party is not a bailiff or a lawyer.
Release the pack and the hold only after the officer chooses.
in_practice.human_gate: The officer decides the path and releases the pack. A hold above the controller's line waits for the controller. For a natural person, including a sole trader or a partnership, the external party is a bailiff, a lawyer, or a party on the Wki register.
data_needed: Invoices, payments and the due dates used
Terms document that was sent to the shipper
Reminder history and collection notes
Filed proofs and dispute status
Wki registration status of any proposed agency
Whether a credit-insurance policy covers the debtor
in_practice.logs_to: The pack in the debtor's SharePoint folder, and the officer's decision and the date on the AFAS dossier.

evidence.claim: Syncasso's module drafts a summons in two minutes. A legal professional reviews it, the bailiff stays responsible for the writ, and handling time falls from 165 to 62 minutes, as Syncasso states it.

Since 1 October 2026 an unregistered party that sends collection reminders for someone else cannot charge collection costs or further interest to a natural person, including a sole trader or a partnership. The debt stands. Bailiffs and lawyers are exempt.
File errors that matter in a later claim include a wrong first letter, miscalculated interest or costs, and terms that were never handed over.

risks: A thin pack repeats the known failure: the interest, the EUR 40, or the terms do not match the file, and the debtor's counsel finds it.
An unregistered agency instructed on a sole trader or a partnership puts the costs and further interest at risk under the Wki. The debt itself remains due.
A credit hold sent in error stops a live lane. The release has to be as clear, and as quick, as the hold.
Syncasso's 165-to-62-minute figure is the vendor's own, on its book of work, and is not a Noordhaven result.
research_questions: How many files were handed to a bailiff, a lawyer or an agency in the last year, and how many hours went into each pack?
For debtors who are natural persons, is every external party Noordhaven uses on the Wki register, or a bailiff or lawyer?
Does Noordhaven have credit insurance on any shipper, and who notifies the insurer today?
Below what balance does the controller prefer to stop, even if the pack is cheap to build?

role.altitude: The week becomes an exception queue after the bank import and a short set of calls with shippers who dispute a load or break a promise. The officer gains the right to time the reminder steps and to place a credit hold inside limits the controller writes down. A write-off, a plan above that limit, or an instruction to a bailiff still needs a second person. The job becomes more expert: what remains is the shipper conversation and the cause of the unpaid invoice.
reach: The bookkeeper's clearing of Rabobank receipts that AFAS did not match, once the officer learns the allocation screen and the VAT coding of a short pay.
The controller's upkeep of credit holds and of limits inside a ceiling the controller sets, once the officer learns that a sole trader's creditworthiness is not something to score.
The FP&A analyst's weekly cash-in input, once the officer learns the categories that forecast already uses in Power BI.
role.ceiling_note: One full-time post at EUR 45 an hour. Calls with shippers who dispute a load, payment plans, and the decision to hand a file to a bailiff stay with this person. A hold has to be visible to planning at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo without a separate call to each shift. The ceiling is the number of disputed shippers one person can know.
skills_to_grow: When BW 6:119a and the EUR 40 compensation belong in a letter, and when the invoice does not support them.
A Wki register check before anyone who is not a bailiff or a lawyer chases a sole trader or a partnership.
How AFAS bank-matching rules are set, so the same miss does not return every import.
Reading a proof of delivery and a damage note well enough to say whether the invoice should stand.
Coding promises and disputes so FP&A can use them in the cash-in forecast.
The EU AI Act limit on creditworthiness scoring of sole-trader hauliers, so a limit stays a documented human decision.
role.ambitious_version: This officer runs order-to-cash for Noordhaven: reminder timing, credit holds inside the controller's ceiling, and a weekly note to Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo and to FP&A on why cash is late, split by damage, waiting time, missing proof, rate and surcharge. The new service is a cash-in forecast that moves when a promise changes, for the Finance Director's close. Demand for that forecast grows if it is cheap to keep: in the 2026 Onguard survey, 81% of Dutch finance and credit professionals explain DSO after the fact, and half plan cash-in no more than two weeks ahead. Smaller seasonal shippers, who today fall behind the large accounts, start to get a timely credit decision, while the officer's own calls stay on the disputed and the strategic accounts.
